answer: Because the atlas audit recomputes usage from the pearl history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. A farm running 184 keys therefore forfeits for 184 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the vine declaration. Each identity declares a compute budget of 497 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
